head: a85bcc5456aba5db8e3616a3b4c164bea7048f74
title: Exclude the query entity explicitly from LightFM similarity results
body:
### Description

LightFM's similarity helpers retrieve N + 1 candidates and discard the first result. When shared features produce tied cosine scores, that first result need not be the query: the query can remain in the returned recommendations while another eligible entity is omitted. Zero feature representations have the same problem.

Exclude the query by its ID before returning the first N sorted candidates. Apply the same small correction to both users and items, preserving cosine scores, descending order and the existing supported N range.

Fixes #2478.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43918186395) checks exact head `a85bcc5456aba5db8e3616a3b4c164bea7048f74` with native LightFM 1.17:

| Environment | Original suite | New cases on baseline | Patched full suite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python 3.10, NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1 | 4 passed, 1 skipped | 12 failed, 12 passed | 28 passed, 1 skipped |
| Python 3.11, NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.13.1 | 4 passed, 1 skipped | 12 failed, 12 passed | 28 passed, 1 skipped |

The sole skip is the existing `test_fitting` marked as flaky upstream. All 24 new cases run. Local Python 3.12 gives the same results.

The tests train actual LightFM models and exercise shared, zero and distinct feature representations, every query ID, and N values 0, 1, 3 and 5. An independent float64 cosine calculation checks returned scores and top-N ordering without prescribing an arbitrary tie order. No model method is mocked.

Black and `git diff --check` pass. The validation workflow builds the unmodified official LightFM 1.17 revision with its Cython command; no dependency build changes are included in this PR.

### History review

Reviewed 1,497 pre-existing upstream PR heads, 69 fork branches and all 28 reachable LightFM utility source versions across 110 commits, including renamed paths and intermediate revisions. Every historical similarity implementation discards the first result by position.
